title: Grateful Dead Live at Kiel Auditorium on 1973-10-29
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> RME Hammerfall Digiface -> Sony Vaio C1VP ->
source: SBD -> Master Reel (7inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> DCassette (Tascam 122mkIII) -> Dat (Panasonic 3700/44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: A superb soundboard mix captures a high‑energy ’73 show, highlighted by an unforgettable Eyes of the World/China Doll pairing and a blazing Other One.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crystal‑clear soundboard source with excellent instrument separation, only marred by brief audience patches on the El Paso. Musically the night bursts with power – the first set’s honky‑tonk swing gives way to a second‑set of jazz‑infused jams, featuring standout performances of Eyes of the World, China Doll, The Other One, Truckin' and Bertha.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer scores (mostly 4‑5 stars) and strong praise for both performance and mix outweigh minor audience patches and occasional mixed comments.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with superb instrument separation; a few rough audience patches (notably on El Paso) and slight pitch drift noted, plus one comment about Bob being too forward in the mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A lively, honky‑tonk first set that builds into a high‑energy second set; jazzy keyboard work and tight group interplay keep the momentum, with seamless transitions especially into China Doll.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as tearing up every solo, offering unique guitar tones (even sounding like a tuba on Mexicali) and delivering an exceptional performance throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: His booming transition into China Doll is highlighted; bass lines are praised for driving the tight jam on Eyes of the World.
band_member_comments.Bob: One reviewer notes Bob's vocals sit too far forward in the mix, but otherwise his contributions are not a focus of criticism.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s jazzy chordal work (McCoy‑Tyner‑like) shines on Truckin' and The Other One; keyboards overall receive high marks for clarity and creativity.
